approved: Ozone Protection and Synthetic Greenhouse Gas (Manufacture Levy) Amendment (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2013
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that repeals the carbon tax.

The package would ban suppliers from charging more than the tax cut justifies for goods like electricity and gas, and give the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) new powers to watch prices and stop false claims about the repeal's effect on prices.
A company breaking the price exploitation rule could face a maximum fine of 6,471 penalty units ($1,100,070), and an individual up to 1,295 penalty units ($220,150).
Creates a new ban on price exploitation tied to the carbon tax repeal for certain key goods.
Gives the ACCC authority to monitor prices before and after the repeal and to check for price exploitation.
Bans companies from making false or misleading statements about the carbon tax repeal's effect on prices.
Businesses that supply key goods such as electricity and gas, and consumers.

Moved the second reading of a companion bill repealing the equivalent carbon tax on manufactured synthetic greenhouse gases, removing the levy for gases manufactured after 1 July 2014 to reduce costs for businesses using refrigeration and air conditioning.

Moved a debate management motion to conclude debate on the Clean Energy Legislation (Carbon Tax Repeal) Bill 2013 and related bills by Thursday this week, arguing the election gave the coalition a mandate with 90 seats to Labor's 55, Labor's worst result since 1903.

Argued against the government's carbon tax repeal bills, saying the decade from 2001 to 2010 was the warmest on record, that Direct Action would cost households an estimated $1,200 a year without a legislated cap on emissions, and noted that under Labor wind power generation trebled and 24,000 renewable energy jobs were created.
